newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAINS FUTURES MOSTLY STEADY OR HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAINS FUTURES MOSTLY STEADY OR HIGHER.

text.p: Feed barley prices began to recover from a four-day plunge in the grain section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Wednesday and traders said could go higher over the next days.
"Barley has a 600 to 800 forints (per tonne) upward potential," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
He added, however, that a drastic price drop in maize prices could pull down barley as well.
Maize futures dominated trade with the July maturity accounting for 365 contracts of the total grains futures turnover of 1,218 contracts or 473 million forints.
"Traders' opinions are divided on which way July prices will go, so both the buying and selling side is strong," Szoke said.
Maize prices rose for March, May and December by 30, 100 and 50 forints respectively, with prices of the old (1996) crop maintaining their inverse positions.

Milling wheat prices finished higher for the March, May, August and October maturities, but Szoke said new (1997) crop prices -- currently between 19,000 and 20,700 forints per tonne, are not based on hard information and could move in either direction.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
